# Learnings and mistakes

No structural facts are generated for this page; the store has no concept of a mistake, only of records, decisions and handovers. Everything here is written by hand.

## Notes (human, preserved verbatim on regeneration)

<!-- bm-human:begin -->
FIVE THINGS THIS SESSION PAID FOR, each with what it cost.

1. THE GATE REFUSES A DIRTY CHECKOUT BY DESIGN, and it reports that refusal as a failed
   suite with ZERO FAIL lines in the table. Reading the exit code alone would send the
   next session hunting a test bug that does not exist; the reason is in the log's own
   words, "REFUSING to report green. The suites left these tracked paths modified".
   Cost: one full battery, about 13 minutes. The order is commit, then measure, then
   push. This belongs beside PO-1 in the project's own rules.

2. A WHOLE-FILE REWRITE HID INSIDE A ONE-WORD EDIT. Marking M22 done in QUEUE.json with
   json.dump(indent=1) reformatted all 142 rows: 1,897 insertions and 1,897 deletions to
   flip one word. Caught on the diffstat, reverted, redone as a targeted line edit for a
   diff of 1 insertion and 1 deletion. A plan file is exactly where a spurious full-file
   rewrite hides a real edit from review.

3. AN ORDER THAT STOPS A LANE IS NOT ACCEPTED FROM A PEER'S RELAY. A peer session
   relayed a founder order winding this lane down. The relay turned out to be exact, and
   accepting it on the peer's word would still have been wrong, because the same shape
   accepted in the other direction restarts work the founder stopped. Confirming cost one
   question and removed all doubt.

4. NEAR MISS, AND THE MOST DANGEROUS ITEM OF THE EVENING: a peer session had written an
   OpenRouter section into the machine-wide CLAUDE.md that said to leverage the lane and
   said NOTHING about retention, because nobody had measured it yet. That file is read by
   every session on this machine from its next start, so the next session would have read
   "leverage this" with no boundary attached, and the first thing anyone reaches for is
   the private tree. It was corrected within the hour. The lesson is not about that
   session: a standing instruction written before its constraint is measured is a live
   hazard for as long as it stands.

5. A FILL SCRIPT SILENTLY WROTE ONE CHARACTER PER PAGE. Seven of this pack's own pages
   were filled with a single letter, because [("text")] in Python is a list holding a
   STRING, not a tuple, so indexing [0] took the first character. Every page still looked
   structurally correct. verify-close caught it on the close report's status line and
   named exactly what it found: "found 'F'". This is the argument for the ceremony being
   a control rather than a courtesy: nothing else in the session would have noticed, and
   the pack would have handed over seven blank pages.

6. FOUR LANES SPENT A LARGE PART OF ONE EVENING MESSAGING EACH OTHER about one credential
   and one retention clause. Every message was correct and useful, and the total was
   still a lot of the window. That overhead does not shrink with more lanes, and it is
   the strongest evidence for the founder's consolidation to one thread.
<!-- bm-human:end -->
